items.title: Guinée : Djénabou Touré annonce de nouvelles élections en 2027
items.description: Alors que le processus électoral de 2026 se poursuit avec les prochaines élections régionales et sénatoriales, le gouvernement guinéen se projette déjà sur de nouvelles échéances. La Ministre de l’Administration du Territoire et de la Décentralisation (MATD), Djénabou Touré, a annoncé, ce vendredi 13 novembre, la tenue d’élections complémentaires en 2027. Elle s'exprimait à l'occasion de la cérémonie de prise de fonction du nouveau Directeur Général des Élections. Dans son intervention, la Ministre a donné un aperçu des prochains rendez-vous électoraux qui attendent le pays l'année prochaine. Parmi les scrutins annoncés figurent notamment les élections dans les nouvelles communes ainsi que l'élection des sénateurs, à la faveur de l'évolution du découpage administratif du territoire national. « L'année prochaine, on aura quelques élections complémentaires, notamment les nouvelles communes, qui, de par la loi, seront créées parce qu'on a déjà des sous-préfectures depuis plus de cinq ans, six ans qui ne sont pas devenues communes », a-t-elle déclaré. Djénabou Touré a ainsi évoqué la nécessité de mettre en conformité certaines collectivités avec les dispositions légales en vigueur. Elle a également fait savoir que le nouveau découpage administratif entraînera la création de nouvelles communes, lesquelles devront à leur tour connaître des échéances électorales. Au-delà des élections communales, la Ministre a annoncé un autre rendez-vous politique majeur : le renouvellement de la représentation sénatoriale dans les nouvelles entités administratives. « Mais également, l'élection des sénateurs après une modification de la loi organique portant règlement intérieur du Sénat », a-t-elle précisé. Selon la Ministre, les nouvelles préfectures ainsi que les deux nouvelles régions seront également concernées par ces élections : « Les nouvelles préfectures et les deux nouvelles régions vont connaître aussi l'élection de leurs sénateurs pour venir compléter le Sénat », a-t-elle expliqué. Cette annonce dessine ainsi les contours d'un nouveau calendrier électoral pour 2027, marqué notamment par la mise en place de nouvelles collectivités territoriales et l'adaptation de la représentation au sein de la chambre haute du Parlement. Djénabou Touré salue le rôle de la Cour suprême Dans la suite de son intervention, la Ministre de l'Administration du Territoire et de la Décentralisation a tenu à rendre hommage à la Cour suprême pour son implication dans le processus électoral qui vient de s'achever. Elle a particulièrement insisté sur l'importance de l'avis consultatif rendu par cette institution juridique, qu'elle considère comme déterminant pour éviter un blocage du processus. Pour Djénabou Touré, cet avis a permis de surmonter plusieurs difficultés d'ordre juridique et administratif qui auraient pu compromettre la finalisation des opérations électorales cette année. « C'est le lieu pour moi de remercier la plus haute institution juridique de notre pays, la Cour suprême, qui a travaillé sans relâche, qui a aidé notre pays à avoir un avis consultatif qui a permis de finaliser le processus électoral cette année », a-t-elle souligné. La Ministre a même estimé que, sans cette intervention de la haute juridiction, le pays aurait pu se retrouver dans une situation de blocage. « Sans l'avis consultatif de la Cour suprême, nous allons nous retrouver dans une situation de blocage, compte tenu de beaucoup de facteurs juridiques mais administratifs également », a-t-elle affirmé. Avant de conclure, Djénabou Touré a renouvelé ses remerciements aux magistrats de cette institution pour leur contribution au dénouement des difficultés rencontrées. « Merci à tous les membres, je dirais, les valeureux magistrats de la Cour suprême pour le travail abattu », a-t-elle conclu. items.title: Controversy looms over new GH₵50 note as Theodosia Okoh’s portrait is disputed
items.description: Controversy has erupted over the newly unveiled GH₵50 banknote, with claims that the portrait on it does not depict Theodosia Salome Okoh, the designer of Ghana’s national flag. The note forms part of the Bank of Ghana’s new Heritage Series, unveiled on Thursday, November 12, 2026, by President John Mahama and Bank of Ghana Governor, Dr Johnson Asiama, at Bank Square in Accra. According to the Central Bank, the GH₵50 note is dedicated to Mrs Okoh, who designed Ghana’s red, gold and green flag with the black star in 1957, and represents the theme of nationalism. However, questions about the identity of the woman depicted on the note emerged shortly after its unveiling, with allegations that the portrait is actually that of Mrs Okoh’s sister, Dr Letitia Obeng. The allegation was first raised prominently by Minority Leader Alexander Afenyo-Markin at a press conference on Thursday evening, where he accused the government of rushing the currency redesign in an attempt to erase the Big Six from Ghana’s history. He said the haste had resulted in what he described as a serious error on the GH₵50 note. “In fact, they were in haste to erase the Big Six from our currency and our history. Out of that haste and hate, we saw them adorning a new fifty-cedi note bearing the name of Theodosia Okoh, but they got her picture wrong and placed on the GH₵50 note a different face,” he said. His comments triggered widespread debate on social media, with users comparing the portrait to photographs of Mrs Okoh. Family member says portrait is of his mother The controversy gained further attention when Dr Eddie Obeng, a supposed nephew of Mrs Okoh and son of Dr Letitia Obeng, publicly disputed the identity of the woman on the note. In a LinkedIn post, Dr Obeng said he was initially delighted to learn that his aunt had been honoured in the new currency series. However, he said he was surprised to discover that the portrait appeared to be that of his mother. Accompanying his post with images of the front and back of the new GH₵50 note, he wrote: “I have a wry smile on my face that won’t go away, and occasionally I shake my head or giggle. So, I heard this morning that my aunt had been honoured in a new series of banknotes issued in Ghana – she’s famous there for designing the country’s flag after independence from Britain. I was very proud and began composing a message to my cousin. Imagine my surprise when I took a look and realised that they have used a picture of my mother instead – she’s famous for being the country’s first lady PhD. You can’t make it up.” Dr Obeng identified the woman in the portrait as his mother, Dr Letitia Obeng, a pioneering Ghanaian scientist and the first Ghanaian woman to earn a PhD. His intervention has added weight to the allegations, particularly because of his direct family connection to both women. His post has since attracted widespread attention, with many social media users citing it as further evidence that the wrong portrait may have been used. The claims have, however, been challenged by a clarification attributed to Beatrice Annan, a member of the Bank of Ghana board and a Presidential Staffer, which has been circulating on social media. Bank official offers explanation In a post on her Facebook page on Thursday, Ms Annan said the portrait was an engraved artistic impression of Mrs Okoh, developed from three authentic photographs of her. She explained that the photographs, two from Mrs Okoh’s younger years and another from later life, were combined to produce an image depicting her as a mature woman. Her hairstyle was also adjusted to achieve a clear outline suitable for engraving. “The Bank of Ghana has noted discussions on social media about the portrait of Mrs Theodosia Salome Okoh, designer of Ghana’s national flag, on the new GH₵50 Heritage Series banknote,” she wrote. She further explained that banknote portraits differ from ordinary photographs because they must meet specific technical requirements for printing, engraving and the incorporation of security features. “A banknote portrait is not an ordinary photograph. It is an engraved artistic rendering created to meet the strict technical requirements of banknote printing. It must be sharp, well lit and rich in fine detail so that it can be engraved, reproduced in raised print and incorporate the security features that protect the note against counterfeiting,” she stated. Ms Annan added that the Bank was engaging Mrs Okoh’s family to explain the process involved in developing the portrait and resolve the concerns. “The aim throughout was to produce a bold, clear and dignified image worthy of her place in our history. The result is the portrait featured on the GH₵50 Heritage Series banknote. The Bank is engaging her family to explain the careful work that went into creating the portrait and resolve the issue,” she said. The response has been questioned Despite Ms Annan’s explanation, the controversy has raised questions about the Bank of Ghana’s official position on the matter. Several hours after her Facebook post, the Central Bank had not published a corresponding statement on its official communication platforms or issued a direct response to the allegations by Mr Afenyo-Markin and Dr Obeng. This has prompted questions about whether Ms Annan’s clarification represents her personal explanation or an officially authorised position of the Bank. Some social media users have also questioned why a matter concerning the integrity of a newly issued national currency was addressed through the personal Facebook page of a Bank official rather than the institution’s established communication channels. With the dispute now involving both political figures and members of Mrs Okoh’s family, attention is turning to the Bank of Ghana for an authoritative explanation of how the portrait was selected and whether it accurately represents the woman whose contribution to Ghana’s national identity the note seeks to honour.

items.title: Orpaillage : à la rencontre d’un jeune burkinabè expulsé de la Guinée
items.description: La fermeture des sites d'orpaillage en Guinee a provoque l'arrivee de milliers de personnes au Mali, parmi lesquelles de nombreux jeunes et adolescents. Pour certains, cette operation a entraîne la perte de leur emploi et de leurs revenus. C'est le cas de David Wari, un Burkinabe de 20 ans, qui attend aujourd'hui son rapatriement. Vetu du maillot de l'equipe nationale du Burkina Faso, David Wari se trouve sur le site d'accueil de Ouezzindougou . Le jeune homme raconte avoir ete surpris par la decision des autorites guineennes de mettre fin aux activites d'orpaillage. « Pendant que nous etions en Guinee, un jour, en train de travailler, on a appris que la Guinee allait arreter l'orpaillage. Nous, on pensait que c'etait une fausse information. Deux mois apres, ils sont venus, en pleine nuit meme, pour nous chasser avec des fusils », temoigne-t-il. « a la recherche d'une vie meilleure » Arrive a Siguiri, en Guinee, il y a environ un an, David explique que la fermeture des ecoles dans son village, en raison de l'insecurite, l'a pousse a chercher du travail a l'etranger. Son activite dans les mines constituait ainsi une source d'espoir pour lui et les autres jeunes partis tenter leur chance. Mais, son avenir financier reste incertain. David explique que sa remuneration dependait d'un employeur installe au Burkina Faso, selon un systeme de paiement annuel. « Mon patron est au Burkina. Je ne saurais vous dire s'il va me payer ou pas dans le contexte actuel. C'est comme ca que le contrat marche entre nous. Au bout d'une annee, les employes rentrent au Burkina pour se faire payer », precise-t-il. Dans l'attente de son retour au Burkina Faso, David Wari nourrit deja un nouveau projet : integrer les rangs de l'armee nationale de son pays. Lire aussi : Quand des orpailleurs expulses de la Guinee se tournent vers les zones minieres du Mali Reguler plutot qu'interdire l'orpaillage Au-dela du sort des personnes expulsees de Guinee, cette situation relance le debat sur la gestion de l'orpaillage artisanal dans la sous-region. Comment lutter efficacement contre l'exploitation illegale de l'or sans priver des milliers de personnes de leurs moyens de subsistance ? Pour le sociologue, professeur Brema Ely Dicko, une interdiction totale et immediate de cette activite pourrait aggraver le chomage. Il preconise plutot une meilleure organisation du secteur, a travers l'application progressive des textes reglementaires deja existants. « C'est difficile peut-etre de prendre des mesures drastiques. Ceci dit, il faut faire comme d'autres pays et mettre en œuvre les textes que nous avons deja concernant la lutte contre l'orpaillage. Ce code minier qui existe avec toutes les strategies nationales », estime-t-il. Le sociologue plaide notamment pour la mise en place de circuits d'achat et de commercialisation de l'or mieux encadres. Selon lui, les autorites devraient favoriser le rachat de la production par des structures maliennes, plutot que de laisser les exploitants dependre de reseaux informels qui alimentent les marches internationaux. Pour Brema Ely Dicko, cette approche permettrait de mieux controler la production aurifere tout en preservant les emplois lies a cette activite. « ca, c'est plutot de la regulation, pas une interdiction dans l'immediat. Parce qu'en le faisant, on met les gens aussi sur le marche du chomage », conclut-il. L’article Orpaillage : à la rencontre d’un jeune burkinabè expulsé de la Guinée est apparu en premier sur Studio Tamani - Informations, débats, magazines : toute l’actualité du Mali, en 5 langues .

items.title: Mali : le Salon BAMEX 2026 ferme ses portes au terme de cinq jours d’échanges et de démonstrations
items.description: Le Salon international de la defense et de la securite (BAMEX 2026) a cloture sa deuxieme edition a Bamako, tenue du 9 au 13 novembre sous le theme « Innovation, renseignement et reactivite : l'Afrique face aux nouveaux defis de la securite globale ». La cooperation technologique et le renforcement des capacites africaines de defense etaient a l'honneur tout au long de l'evenement qui a vu la participation de plusieurs delegations internationales, dont celle de la Russie, qui ont presente divers equipements de defense et ont echange leurs experiences et expertises. Selon le directeur du salon, Harun Sarac, l'evenement ambitionne de rapprocher les industriels internationaux des decideurs africains rendant ainsi possible le transfert de technologies, la maintenance des equipements et les perspectives de production locale. « Demo Day », une journee spectaculaire pour reveler le potentiel des technologies militaires Les delegations militaires malienne et internationales etaient au rendez-vous du « Demo Day » sur le site de Tanabougou. L'evenement etait tres attendu car il permettait d'evaluer et de constater la puissance de feu, la maniabilite et la fiabilite des equipements et du materiel militaire presentes lors du BAMEX 2026. Il s'est traduit par une sorte de spectacle tres intense, rythme par les tirs nourris des engins de combat allant des blindes lourds aux blindes legers en passant par les drones et les diverses gammes d'armements individuels et collectifs. Des manœuvres tactiques, ainsi que des essais de tirs ont ete effectues par des militaires ou des invites de marque. Par cette journee de demonstration, le BAMEX 2026 fournit un banc d'essai concret faisant la particularite du salon, qui risque de devenir un evenement incontournable dans la region pour exposer les productions militaires et en juger les capacites operationnelles sur le terrain. N'Geleni : le Mali presente son premier drone concu localement Presente comme un signe du genie technologique militaire malien, le drone N'Geleni, entierement imagine, assemble et developpe par des competences maliennes est qualifie de « prouesse d'ingenierie » par la presse locale. Cet aeronef sans pilote est propulse par un moteur a essence monte sur un fuselage a l'architecture qualifiee d'audacieuse. Ces caracteristiques permettent a l'engin de beneficier d'une excellente autonomie de vol et d'une capacite d'emport adaptee aux caracteristiques geographiques tres etendues du territoire malien. Outre ses capacites militaires, le N'Geleni ouvre aussi des perspectives concretes et prometteuses, toujours selon la presse malienne, en matiere d'usages civils et economiques. Le drone a rencontre un succes populaire certain aupres des jeunes et des ingenieurs maliens, dans la mesure ou il concretise les visees de recherche appliquee et de souverainete technologique tant convoitees et defendues par les gouvernements de la region.

items.title: CAN 2027 : l’Éthiopie fait tomber le Mozambique et ouvre la voie au Sénégal
items.description: L’Éthiopie a créé la sensation dans le groupe J des éliminatoires de la CAN 2027. Battue lors de ses deux premières sorties, la sélection éthiopienne est allée s’imposer à Maputo face au Mozambique (0-1). Un succès précieux, qui relance les Walya dans la course à la qualification et fait les affaires du Sénégal. Les Éthiopiens ont ainsi décroché leurs premiers points dans ces éliminatoires, tandis que les Mambas manquent l’occasion de conforter leur deuxième place. Avec cette défaite, le Mozambique reste bloqué à quatre points, derrière le Sénégal, solide leader avec sept unités après sa large victoire (4-1) contre le Soudan, jeudi, au stade Léopold Sédar Senghor. Les Lions disposent désormais de trois points d’avance sur les Mozambicains et de quatre sur les Walya. Le Soudan, lui aussi crédité de trois points, ferme la marche. Le déplacement à Khartoum, lundi, sera donc une étape importante pour les hommes de Patrick Vieira afin de sécuriser la qualification. Un succès les porterait à dix points et les placerait en position très favorable pour décrocher l’une des deux places qualificatives de la poule J. C.G.D

items.description: This article was featured in the One Story to Read Today newsletter. Sign up for it here. J oe Biden has a favorite saying that he has attributed to various family members over the years, most often to his mother: Joey , she’d tell him, never bow; never bend; never kneel; never yield. That sentiment runs through his nearly 500-page memoir, as he recounts his four years as president, his decision to run for reelection, and his attempt to stay in the race after the worst presidential-debate performance in American history. “Today there is no shortage of people who think I blindly raced to run again. Driven by ambition. Selfishness. Unaware of the concerns about my age,” he states, accurately. “I knew better than anyone how old I was. I knew what I was—and wasn’t—capable of doing. I carefully monitored how I was meeting the demands of the job. And there is not a single example of me failing to handle my responsibilities.” Biden, as you can tell, is neither reflective nor repentant. He does not concede mistakes, and seems to regret almost nothing. He believes he was right to run for a second term, wishes he had been given the chance for a second debate with Donald Trump, and still insists he maintained the support of average voters even as party leadership pressed him to get out of the race. Evidence to the contrary never intrudes on Biden’s recounting of his last acts in politics after a half-century-long career. To make the case that his debate debacle should not have been disqualifying, he notes that Barack Obama had had a “terrible” outing during his first debate in 2012 and had left it to his vice president to “stop the bleeding. Which I did.” The argument may strain credulity, but it is quintessentially Biden. Several books have covered this ground—including Jill Biden’s View From the East Wing , which was released in June. But Joe Biden’s memoir, Promise Me, America , is the fullest account of his thinking in his own words. One of the most revealing passages comes in the last third of the book, after Biden narrates key episodes of his presidency. With Trump the likely Republican nominee, Biden comes up with a very Trumpian justification for why he needed to run against him, with echoes of Trump’s 2016 vow, “I alone can fix it”: “I believed I was the best person to do it. I was the only person who had ever beaten Donald Trump. And I felt I was the best person to do it again.” Biden is aware of the second-guessing that arose from that choice. He just doesn’t give it any credence. “I had asked the hard questions of myself. Could I do it? Did I still want to do it? Was there anyone else to do it?” he writes. “I answered that yes, physically I would be able to do the job. And not only did I want to do it, I wanted to do it more than ever.” Yet he also suggests his decision to run was selfless, not selfish. He may have openly coveted the presidency for most of his life, but he insists that a single term would have been satisfactory. “The easiest thing for me to do would have been to say I wouldn’t run again. It would have been far easier for me, and for my family. But I felt an obligation to run. I felt I had set the country on the right path.” And he had, in fact, defeated Trump in 2020, winning what he termed a “battle for the soul of this nation,” and the first half of the book is a reminder of some of the sweeping legislation that he shepherded through Congress. The decisions he made four years later, though, helped Trump return to political power. It is no small irony that the book is coming out during a moment of Democratic jubilation, one in which the party seems eager to move beyond what it once was. But now Democrats are being visited by a Ghost of the Party’s Past. The book is a reminder of the painful intramural debates that marked an ultimately failed attempt to hold the presidency. It is also a reminder of how stubborn Biden remains, how the man who always felt burned and resentful of Democrats who overlooked him still has some scores to settle. Biden knew he was old. His voice had thinned, and he had a tendency of misstating places and names. But his gait, in particular, had become such a visual reminder of his age that it came up when Mitt Romney and his family were over at the White House in May 2022 for a private tour. The senator pulled the president aside for a quiet moment. “Pump your arms,” Romney told him. “Excuse me?” Biden responded. “You’re holding your hands stiffly by your side when you walk. Pump your arms and you’ll look more energetic and confident,” Romney instructed. Biden thought it was good advice—delivered via the long-lost art of bipartisan decency—and he tried to take it. But it also became an example of Biden’s reluctance to see his age and cognitive decline as a reason he couldn’t run for reelection, as if pumping his arms vigorously enough might cause voters to overlook his aging body and mind. “I believed the experience and the wisdom I had gained over fifty years in public life outweighed the obvious weaknesses of age,” he writes. [ Read: A different kind of fading president ] He points to two moments that convinced him he could run again. The first was his 2023 State of the Union address, which he says received “universal, enthusiastic support from my fellow Democrats.” The second was his unannounced trip to Kyiv two weeks later—a risky foray into a war zone but one that, in Biden’s telling, included packed PB&J sandwiches and, as a longtime Amtrak rider, a fascination with Ukraine’s rail system. He felt that he had addressed concerns that he lacked the vigor to run for reelection. He recounts his advisers being in agreement before his April 2023 announcement that he was running again, during a “speak now or forever hold your peace” meeting in the Treaty Room. Ron Klain sat on the couch next to him, Jen O’Malley Dillon nearby. Jill Biden urged everyone to give their unvarnished views. Mike Donilon said the polling during his presidency had been remarkably consistent. “There was no demurral or dissent,” Biden reports of the nine people he listed in the room with him. “I was in.” And he writes of how, as he surveyed his party, he saw talent and ambition on the horizon, but the best Democratic candidate for president, it was clear, remained Joe Biden. “I did not believe any one of them was a stronger candidate than me, or had a better chance of winning in 2024,” he writes, with more than a hint of defensiveness. “You can dismiss that assessment if you want. But I know the process I went through. I made a thoughtful, careful, rigorous judgment.” He argues that the absence of a strong challenger is proof that the party agreed with his self-assessment. “Anyone who was scared off from running has no business being president.” He cites his strong primary wins, even though he faced little serious opposition. “I had it on good authority that several big names in Democratic politics had looked at running. They held meetings and took polls and talked to donors and to potential staff. If they thought I was weak or vulnerable, they would have taken their shot. But they didn’t,” he writes. “The press and pundits kept talking about how weak I was. But every purportedly serious candidate decided not to run against me because I was too strong.” B iden spends surprisingly little time dissecting the debate that sent his campaign careening to its inevitable end. Jill Biden, in her own memoir, wrote that she thought her husband was short-circuiting, was having a stroke, or perhaps had been drugged . Strangely, Biden doesn’t address his wife’s speculation, even to dismiss it. He simply says: “I lost my train of thought.” That’s it. This is what Biden believes—or, more to the point, what he wants the world to believe. The problem for Biden is that the debate was actually broadcast nationally and seen by millions of intelligent citizens who may now crave deeper reflection from him on that consequential moment. Biden recalls having spent roughly five days preparing for the debate, staying in the presidential cabin at Camp David and doing mock sessions with his advisers. He was feeling sick, but had tested negative for COVID. The debate came after a long stretch of travel and followed the grueling trial and gun-charge convictions of his son, Hunter. “In the end, they failed to break Hunter. But I would be lying if I didn’t admit that they took a piece out of me,” he writes. He arrived at the debate hall shortly before it began, and, he writes, “It didn’t feel right from the start.” He knew it had gone badly, but many times first debates don’t go as planned for incumbent presidents. He left the stage thinking he would be debating Trump again, and he would improve. “Lots of presidents had bad debates,” he writes. “The difference was that every other president was given the chance to redeem themselves in a second debate. As it turned out, that chance would not be available to me.” [ Watch: The protective ‘politburo’ that hid Biden’s decline ] He attributes his decision to drop out not to factors that he himself was responsible for, but to a remorseless, all-consuming media narrative, and to party leaders who bought into this defeatist narrative: “They would say that whether I stayed in the race was my decision to make. And they would respect whatever decision I made. In reality, the only decision they would respect would be my decision to exit the race.” Former House Speaker Nancy Pelosi was one of the ringleaders, Biden says, meeting with him privately at the White House to urge him to reassess. “Publicly she was still saying it was my decision to make. But privately she was working furiously behind the scenes to get elected officials and Biden delegates to defect,” he writes. Senate Majority Leader Chuck Schumer came to his beach house in Delaware, to implore him to do the same. Still, Biden was reluctant. “I wasn’t living in a dream world. Here’s where I was living: I had won the Democratic nomination for president. And I had won it decisively,” he writes. “I believed I was the best person to lead the world.” He and Schumer argued over the polling, and Biden recounts that he took it personally that old allies were turning on him. “I told Schumer he had a lot of gumption (I may have said it differently at the time), coming to my home and telling me to get out of the race,” he writes. “Loyalty matters to me. If I give you my word, I stick with you. If I say I’m with you, I’m with you to the end.” He eventually determined that he could remain the nominee, but he would be acting against the wishes of top party leaders and donors. It would divide the party. He asked Donilon, his longtime adviser, to draft a statement. Then Biden slept on it. “Believe it or not, I slept well that night,” he writes. The next day he announced his decision to withdraw, then began calling a long list of allies to thank them. In the book, he lists their names and the precise times he called them. There are union presidents and governors, senators and House members. He called Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez at 3:09 p.m. and Bill Clinton at 3:14 p.m. His 7:06 p.m. call to Gretchen Whitmer , he recalls, went to voicemail. Two names are conspicuously absent from the many calls he reported making: He never reached out to Pelosi, and, notably, he does not list Obama, the man who gave him the biggest break of his professional life, as one of those he called. The president of Steelworkers International? Yes, but not Obama. He writes that he was firmly against a contested primary to replace him: “Any contested open fight would have been seen as an attempt to block the first Black female vice president from the top of the ticket, and it would have split the party.” Instead, he fully supported his vice president, Kamala Harris, as the nominee. He largely glosses over the 107 days of her campaign , including moments in which she was reluctant to criticize or distance herself from him. “She inherited a united party. And she created an enthusiastic one: Kamala electrified the country,” he writes. “She was a first-rate candidate. She performed masterfully in her debate with President Trump. She was great on the stump. She was a fundraising machine. I was proud of her and the campaign she ran.” After she lost, Biden invited his predecessor and successor to the Oval Office, but the encounter became somewhat disorienting. Trump was chatty, surprising Biden with a tone so friendly and even fawning that Biden thought Trump might be putting him on. “You know, Joe, if it weren’t for politics, I believe we’d be good friends,” Biden recalls Trump telling him. “If it weren’t for politics, we’d spend all our time golfing together.” Trump, Biden writes, relayed that he was relieved to not have had to run against him. In Biden’s telling, he eventually cut Trump off, confused why he was buttering him up, and began talking about global affairs. The meeting, scheduled for 30 minutes, lasted nearly two hours. (This genial version of Trump also came across four years earlier when Trump left a letter for Biden in the Oval Office in which he channeled history, wished him well, and wrote: “I know you will be true to yourself and the American people.” It was written two weeks after January 6, 2021, and as he continued claiming Biden hadn’t actually won.) [ Joe Biden: What Trump did on January 6 ‘should follow him to his grave’ ] T he epilogue of the book addresses Biden’s discovery last year that he has an aggressive form of prostate cancer that has metastasized to his bones. He rebuts some speculation that he had kept the diagnosis hidden to downplay concerns about his health or age during his presidency—“For anyone to think I would try to ignore or hide a cancer ravaging my body is absurd”—and says he wishes he had been tested earlier. “As of this writing, I’m feeling good,” he writes. On Sunday night, Biden offered a glimpse into the state of his health, writing on social media that “some days are better than others” and that he won’t be able to do as many events related to the book’s release as he had once planned. “I’m hopeful the words on the page speak for themselves,” he wrote. Biden closes the book with another saying from his family, one that he often cited during his presidency and that he channeled while trying to stay in a race he would ultimately leave. “When I was a kid, whenever something bad would happen, I could count on my dad to say, ‘When you get knocked down, get up,’” he writes. “Until I’m counted out for the last time, I’ll keep getting up. And America will too.” In an interview with People magazine published this week, he said that if his cancer diagnosis had come while he was in the White House, he would have resigned: “I would’ve not gone forward, because I don’t think an 80-year-old man with cancer should be running.“ Since that wasn’t the case, he believed, “on an objective basis I was the best-equipped person to do the job.” Remarkably, nowhere in the book does he acknowledge—even ruefully, or in passing—what the reader instantly comprehends: If he had run in 2024 and won, he would now be a visibly frail 83-year-old man, fighting a vicious form of cancer while trying to fulfill the endless responsibilities of the American presidency.

items.title: Explosion d'une voiture à Moscou : l'ex-Premier ministre ukrainien attribue à Kiev la tentative d'assassinat visant son ancien conseiller
items.description: L'ancien Premier ministre ukrainien Nikolaï Azarov a commente a RT l'explosion de la voiture de son ancien conseiller Sergueï Zavorotny, survenue a Moscou, en declarant etre « choque » : « Je n'aurais jamais pu imaginer qu'un attentat aussi barbare puisse etre perpetre contre un homme pacifique, âge de 72 ans, journaliste, exercant un metier tout a fait pacifique. Il s'agit, en somme, d'un acte terroriste », a-t-il souligne. Azarov s'est dit convaincu que l'explosion de la voiture a ete perpetree par les services secrets ukrainiens et leurs agents sur le territoire russe. Selon lui, le principal motif etait l'activite journalistique de Zavorotny, qui visait a denoncer les agissements du regime de Kiev. « Et le fait qu'un engin explosif ait ete place ne visait certainement pas a intimider, ni a adresser un quelconque avertissement. Cela visait a tuer cette personne », a-t-il ajoute a Soloviov.Live. L'ancien Premier ministre ukrainien a egalement evoque l'etat de sante de son ancien assistant, qu'il a qualifie de critique. Qualifiant ses blessures de tres graves, il lui a souhaite un prompt retablissement. L'explosion de la voiture s'est produite dans la matinee du 13 novembre dans le sud de Moscou. La Direction generale des enquetes du Comite d'enquete de Russie a confirme que la victime etait le journaliste international Sergueï Zavorotny. Il a ete transporte dans un hopital moscovite, ou il est actuellement soigne. Selon une source de RT au sein des forces de l'ordre, l'homme a perdu un bras, souffre d'une commotion cerebrale et de fractures. D'apres des temoins oculaires, l'explosion a provoque des secousses dans les immeubles d'habitation voisins, et la voiture a ete projetee a plusieurs metres. Le Comite d'enquete de Russie a ouvert une enquete penale pour tentative de meurtre.

items.title: Emefiele: Court admits Supreme Court judgment in alleged $4.5bn fraud trial
items.description: An Ikeja Special Offences Court on Friday admitted a certified copy of a Supreme Court judgment linking former CBN Governor, Godwin Emefiele, to forfeited properties. Justice Rahman Oshodi admitted the judgment as Exhibit L after overruling objections by Emefiele’s defence counsel. Emefiele is facing a 19-count charge bordering on alleged gratification, corrupt demands and abuse of office involving $4.5 billion and N2.8 billion. His co-defendant, Henry Omoile, is facing a three-count charge of alleged unlawful acceptance of gifts. Oshodi ruled that the certified true copy of the Supreme Court judgment was admissible as a public document. He said the fact that only the lead judgment was tendered did not render it incomplete or inadmissible. The judge also addressed concerns about the prosecution’s reliance on a civil judgment in the ongoing criminal trial. He, however, restricted its use to establishing what the Supreme Court had decided in the previous proceedings. He stressed that the judgment could not constitute evidence for or against any party in the ongoing trial. “It has been well settled that court judgments are only used when tendered in a trial to determine and confirm what was actually decided in the case. “They are not used as evidence given in them for or against any of the parties therein,” Oshodi said. The Director of Public Prosecutions of the Federation, Mr Rotimi Oyedepo (SAN), had tendered the document through EFCC investigator, Mr Alvan Gurumnaan. However, Emefiele’s lead counsel, Mr Ojo Olalekan (SAN), opposed its admissibility, arguing that only four justices signed the judgment. He maintained that Supreme Court decisions were ordinarily delivered by panels of five or seven justices. Ojo also argued that the judgment arose from non-conviction forfeiture proceedings and was irrelevant to the prosecution’s case. Counsel to Omoile, Mr Adeyinka Kotoye (SAN), aligned himself with the objections and urged the court to reject the document. Kotoye argued that admitting the judgment could undermine the principle of estoppel and the defendants’ presumption of innocence. He also questioned the prosecution’s decision to introduce the document after proceedings had begun. Responding, Oyedepo argued that the document was a duly certified Supreme Court decision admissible under Sections 102 and 104 of the Evidence Act. Following the ruling, Gurumnaan faced cross-examination by Emefiele’s counsel over his role in the investigation. The witness said he personally obtained statements, analysed bank statements and coordinated other members of the investigation team. He confirmed interviewing Zenith Bank Managing Director, Dr Ebenezer Onyeagwu, but could not immediately recall whether a statement was obtained. Gurumnaan said the investigation involved hundreds of interviews with CBN officials, commercial bank employees and personnel of other government agencies. Oshodi adjourned the case until Dec. 17 for continuation of cross-examination. The post Emefiele: Court admits Supreme Court judgment in alleged $4.5bn fraud trial appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Nigeria’s Solana joins Sony’s Since ’93 Records, releases new EP Girl From The West
items.description: Lagos-born singer Solana has signed with Since ’93 Records, the label and management group has revealed exclusively to Billboard U.K. The deal sees the emerging Nigerian artist join the U.K.-based company, which has also been home to African artists including Tems and Tyla. Solana is developing ‘YoruPop,’ a sound combining the Yoruba language and influences with synth-pop, Fuji music, R&B and electronic production. Solana’s signing aligns with the release of her debut EP, Girl From The West, due this Friday (Nov. 13). The artist dropped her breakthrough single “Okunkun” (translating to “darkness” in Yoruba) earlier this year and has since received co-signs across social media from the likes of SZA, Tyla, Doechii and Little Simz. She has also been named a Spotify EQUAL Africa Ambassador. “Super excited to partner with Since ‘93 and the Sony Music team for this next chapter,” Solana said in a press statement. “Thank you to all my lanterns for your support, we’re bringing the world into our YoruPop universe. I’m excited to share my world with you, Girl From The West.” Riki Bleau, co-president of Since ‘93, added, “We are excited to announce the Queen of YoruPop, Solana, as a new signing to Since ’93, continuing a rich tradition of supporting exceptional female talent from Africa like Tems and Tyla.” Since ‘93 began as Avant Garde Music in 2012, founded by Bleau. It focused on artist management and music publishing working with Emeli Sandé, Labrinth and Sam Smith, among others. In 2018, the firm relaunched as a new label with Sony Music, with early signings including the BRIT-winning rapper Aitch and Fredo, who scored a No. 5 mixtape on the Official U.K. Albums Chart with Tables Turn later that year. The current Since ‘93 roster includes Cat Burns — who enjoyed a star turn on BBC’s The Celebrity Traitors last year alongside releasing her second LP, How To Be Human — alongside the Elton John-backed songwriter Nectar Woode, and Shallipopi, a singer and rapper from Nigeria. In recognition of his tenure at Since ‘93, where he serves alongside fellow co-president Glen Aitkins, Bleau was named to Billboard’s 2026 Global Power Players List. Speaking about the honor, he said, “I’m grateful to Billboard for this recognition and to be among so many incredible ‘doers’ from our industry. “We’ve worked hard to create a culture and space at Since ‘93 where artists and creatives feel empowered and are at the center of everything we do. I’m thankful to every talent who allowed me to be a part of their journey. I’m proud of our work, and proud to lead the U.K.’s most successful black-led label and will continue to support the next generation of talent from all over the world.”

items.title: Customs intercepts concealed textiles and 10 motorbikes at Techiman checkpoint
items.description: Officers of the Customs Division at Techiman have intercepted 97 bales of imitation wax prints and 10 unpacked Yamaha Aerox motorbikes concealed in a Burkina Faso-registered cargo truck at the Techiman checkpoint. A DAF XF cargo truck, with registration number BF2798G303, was stopped on Thursday, November 5, 2026, by Customs officers and during a search, officers discovered textile bales hidden beneath dry okro powder and empty glass bottles. The vehicle was then escorted to the Sunyani Regional Office for a full examination. The inspection uncovered 97 bales of imitation wax prints, amounting to 58,200 yards of fabric, as well as 10 new, unpacked 155cc Yamaha Aerox motorbikes. Customs officers described the goods as uncustomed, meaning the required import duties and clearance procedures had not been completed. The estimated duty on the textile consignment is GH¢465,186.90. This was based on an FOB value of $52,962, together with freight, insurance, import duty, VAT and various levies and charges. The seized items were covered by Notices of Seizure Nos. 0015388, 0015392, 0015393, 0015394 and 0015395, all issued on November 11, 2026. The notices cite provisions of the Customs Act, 2015 (Act 891) and describe the goods as liable to forfeiture. Some of the seizure notices identified Sansadogo Mohammed in connection with the motorbikes, while another notice was addressed to “Dabil” and “Perpetual” in relation to the textile consignment. The documents stated that any person wishing to challenge the forfeiture must submit a written claim within one calendar month. If no claim is filed, the goods may be treated as lawfully forfeited and disposed of as directed by the Commissioner. The goods have since been deposited at the Sunyani Regional Office state warehouse pending further action. The interception underscores ongoing Customs enforcement against the concealment and undeclared importation of goods through inland

items.title: Interior Minister cautions communities against confronting security agencies during operations
items.description: The Minister for the Interior, Muntaka Mubarak, has cautioned communities against confronting security personnel during operations, warning that such encounters could result in needless loss of life and injuries. He says while security agencies must be held accountable for their conduct, the public must also cooperate with them in the discharge of their duties. Addressing a gathering at the commissioning of a renovated interrogation centre, a new forensic laboratory and the presentation of 111 vehicles by President Mahama to the Bureau of National Investigations (BNI), the Minister stressed the need for communities to respect security operations rather than obstruct them. “Your Excellency, I want to take this opportunity to caution communities against unnecessarily confronting our security agencies during operations. While we must hold our security agencies accountable, communities must understand that security operations must be respected and cooperated with, rather than confronted. Such confrontations sometimes lead to needless loss of life and injuries,” he said. The Minister also reaffirmed government’s commitment to strengthening the country’s security institutions through investments in operational capacity, infrastructure, technology and logistical resources. He, however, emphasised that these investments must be matched by professionalism, discipline, integrity and responsible conduct. “The confidence of the Ghanaian people in our security institutions must remain central to everything that we do,” he stated. He further called for stronger regional cooperation, intelligence sharing and coordinated responses to security threats, noting that Ghana’s security is closely linked to stability across the West African sub-region. “A secure Ghana contributes significantly to a more stable West Africa, particularly among our neighbouring countries,” he said. The Minister urged the leadership and personnel of the Bureau to make effective use of the newly commissioned facilities and additional operational vehicles to improve their work.

items.title: Why I lied about having cancer – Blessing CEO
items.description: By Wasiu Rokibat Nigerian social media personality Blessing Okoro, popularly known as Blessing CEO, has sparked fresh reactions after admitting that she falsely claimed to have breast cancer which in turn led to financial assistance from members of the public. The relationship influencer made the revelation during an interview with social media activist Martins Vincent Otse, better known as VeryDarkMan. Speaking during the interview, Blessing explained that although medical examinations discovered a lump in her breast, the result showed that it was not cancerous. However, she admitted that she deliberately presented the condition as cancer to attract sympathy from fans. In her words, “I do not have cancer. I had gone for a check-up and they found a lump in my breast, but it was not cancerous. I took advantage of that and told the public that the lump was cancerous. I played an emotional game.” According to her, she initially suggested that she might sell some of her personal belongings, including her car and house, before members of the public encouraged her to share her bank details for financial assistance. Blessing also disclosed that donations began coming in from different individuals but stopped after VeryDarkMan publicly questioned her cancer claims and demanded evidence of her diagnosis. “People had empathy, I did not come out to beg for funds. I played an emotional game. I wanted funds but I didn’t come out directly to ask for funds. I started with pretending I wanted to sell my personal belongings, my house, my car; It was fans who reached out to me in my DM, asking me to put out my account number; that’s when I put out my account number.” “The donation was rolling in, until VeryDarkMan came and say you people cannot be donating money for Blessing when there is no evidence. Immediately, VeryDarkMan made that video, the donation stopped. I am not proud of what I did.” The confession has renewed public attention to the controversy, which began in March 2026 when the influencer announced that she had breast cancer and appealed for financial support. She had previously acknowledged receiving about N13 million in donations but maintained that there had been confusion surrounding her medical condition. The matter also attracted the attention of the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC), which arraigned her over alleged offences connected to the fundraising campaign. She pleaded not guilty to the charges. Vanguard News The post Why I lied about having cancer – Blessing CEO appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Le rapport diagnostic du PDC de la commune Kéran 2 validé
items.description: Kantè, 13 nov. (ATOP)- Le rapport diagnostic du Plan de développement communal (PDC) de la commune Kéran 2, a été validé le vendredi 13 novembre à Atalotè, à environ 13 km à l’ouest de Kantè. Présidée par le secrétaire général de la préfecture, Bello Séfiou, cette cérémonie marque une étape dans la suite du processus d’élaboration du PDC de la commune Kéran 2. L’objectif est de renforcer l’adhésion des divers acteurs locaux dans le processus d’élaboration du PDC en les impliquant davantage dans la collecte, l’analyse et le traitement des données. Afin de dresser un état exhaustif des lieux, la méthodologie s’est appuyée sur les données primaires obtenues auprès des ménages et des acteurs socio-économiques locaux. Quant aux données secondaires, elles ont porté sur l’historique, la démographie, le profil socio-économique et culturel de la commune. La prochaine étape du processus est relative à la définition des visions et orientations stratégiques en vue de la phase de programmation. La cérémonie a connu la présence du maire de la commune Kéran 2, Datibe Adjin et d’un aménagiste au ministère délégué en charge du Développement local, Dr Boudou Mintre. L’élaboration de ce diagnostic a été financée par la Société autonome de financement de l’entretien routier (SAFER). ATOP/PAP/MD

items.title: Dead Men Can Teach: Why Ghana’s Medical Schools are running out of bodies
items.description: Some months ago, a sister of one of my mentors passed away at the Korle Bu Teaching Hospital in Accra. There was no funeral because she, knowing her illness was terminal, chose to donate her body to the University of Ghana Medical School for medical research. This was my first personal encounter with such a donation. During the procedures related to the body bequest, the doctor in charge explained the challenges in securing cadavers (bodies) for medical training and mentioned that limited admissions of medical students in Ghana are partly due to this issue and not just infrastructure. This inspired me to write this article. Consider what a body represents to medical science. It is not just tissue and bone. It is a complete textbook, a laboratory that teaches and a final teacher whose lessons endure in every doctor it helps train. When a patient dies of a disease that medicine does not yet fully understand, their body holds answers. When a new medication is developed, its effects on human physiology must be studied in human bodies and not just in computer models or animal subjects. When old medicines need revision because diseases evolve or populations change, researchers must see how those medicines interact with human tissue, organs and systems. Most of the medical researchers in Ghana face this challenge. Without fresh bodies, they cannot study the effects of emerging diseases like new viral strains or resistant infections. They cannot test how new medications affect organs in real human subjects. They cannot refine surgical techniques that might save thousands of lives. Korle Bu’s Medical School, like others across the country, has historically relied heavily on unclaimed bodies. Thus, those left in mortuaries with no family to claim them. But this source is no longer reliable. Mortuaries are overwhelmed, and even unclaimed bodies are often too decomposed or otherwise unsuitable for meaningful study. The hospital has had to conduct mass burials of unclaimed bodies, removing them from any possibility of contributing to medical education. The Anatomy of a Medical Student’s Education Imagine the scene: one hundred first-year medical students gather around a single dissection table. They crowd, struggle for position, peer over shoulders and others. The professor points to a nerve, a vessel or a muscle, and most of these students cannot see. Then the situation means that those at the back would have to rely on textbooks and imagination. This is not an exaggeration. In Ghanaian medical schools, the student-to-cadaver ratio is a big challenge. Some institutions report having only a handful of cadavers for entire cohorts of hundreds of students. The result is that students learn anatomy through models, digital simulations and textbook diagrams, which, although very important, cannot be substituted for what is done with the cadaver. Cadaveric dissection remains the gold standard for learning human anatomy. It teaches not only structure but how bodies differ from one another. It teaches surgical technique, respect for the human body and the three-dimensional relationships that no flat image can convey. A study conducted at the University of Health and Allied Sciences (UHAS) in Ghana on 513 health science students – medicine, nursing, midwifery, pharmacy and allied health revealed that only 74.1% of these students had heard of body bequeathal, 98.3% agreed body bequeathal was important, and only 39.6% knew the requirements and processes of body bequeathal. The paper also says 214 students (41.7%) said they had no idea what was required in the process. It is obvious that there was a high awareness of the importance of body bequeathal but very low procedural knowledge, as most were unwilling to donate their body. A Culture of Funerals, A Shortage of Teachers Ghanaian culture, particularly among the Akan and many other ethnic groups, places a strong significance on funeral rites and the treatment of the dead. The body is not only a vessel that has stopped working. It is a site of ritual, a conduit for ancestral blessings and a subject of communal mourning. Funerals in Ghana are detailed, expensive and protracted affairs. Bodies are bathed, dressed, displayed and buried with ceremony. To suggest that a loved one’s body be given to medical students for dissection, which means to be cut, studied, and eventually disposed of, can feel like a violation of cultural and spiritual obligations. This is not a small or dismissible concern. These are deeply held beliefs about the afterlife, about respect, about the relationship between the living and the dead. Any conversation about body donation in Ghana must begin with acknowledgement of this cultural weight and not dismissal of it. Yet there is a tension worth examining. The same culture that insists on detailed funerals also values healing, community and the preservation of life. If a body can no longer benefit the deceased, could it benefit the living? If a funeral honours a life that was lived, could a donation honour a life that could still be saved? The Law Already Allows It Ghana’s Anatomy Act of 1965 (Act 280) provides a legal framework for body donation. Section 3 explicitly allows any individual to direct, either in writing or verbally before two witnesses during their final illness, that their body be used for medical education and research. Section 2 permits executors or those with lawful possession of a body to allow such use, unless the deceased expressed a contrary desire or a surviving spouse or relative objects. The law is permissive but not proactive. It does not actively encourage donation, does not create an accessible system for willing donors and does not provide the cultural and religious engagement needed to shift deeply held norms. As a result, Ghana has only two institutions with any form of body donation programme, and these receive an average of just five and two bodies per year, respectively. In a country with multiple medical schools and thousands of students, this is a drop in an empty bucket. The Way Forward: A Call for Courageous Conversation What would it take to change this? The answer must be many-sided, culturally sensitive, and sustained. First, leadership from chiefs and religious leaders is essential. As research on community responses to health crises in Ghana has shown, when traditional and religious authorities endorse changes to deeply held practices, communities are far more likely to follow. If the National House of Chiefs, the Christian Council and Islamic leadership publicly endorsed body donation as an act of service and healing, the cultural calculus would shift. Second, hospitals must create accessible and dignified donation programmes: Individuals who know they are dying, whether from terminal illness or old age, should have a clear, compassionate pathway to bequeath their bodies. The process must be respectful, transparent and honoured with acknowledgement and gratitude. Third, medical schools must invest in public education. The fact that nearly all health science students support body donation in principle but few know how to do it reveals a massive gap in information. This gap extends to the general public. Educational campaigns, testimonies from families who have donated, and visible memorials to donors can help normalise the practice. Fourth, the legal structure for body bequeathal should be strengthened. Parliament has already recognised the need for updated legislation on organ and tissue donation, noting that only 10 per cent of global transplantation needs are met and that the African region is far behind. The same legislative energy should be applied to body donation for education, with provisions for donor registries, family consent protocols and protections against commercial exploitation. Finally, we must reframe the conversation. Body donation is not abandonment of the dead. It is, in a great sense, the ultimate act of healing. A body that teaches a medical student to recognise a tumour, to perform a delicate surgery, to understand a disease does not lie idle in the ground. It works. The Teacher Who Never Speaks In medical schools around the world, cadavers are often called the “silent teachers.” They do not lecture. They do not explain. They simply are. And by being, they teach what no book can. In Ghana, we have the opportunity to create a culture where donation is not taboo but honoured. Where a family’s grief is joined by a community’s gratitude. Where the dead continue to serve the living not through memory alone but through medicine. Korle Bu Teaching Hospital needs bodies. Ghana’s medical students need bodies. The patients of tomorrow, that is, the ones who will survive because a doctor learned from someone who gave their body to science, need those bodies too. The question is whether we are brave enough to have the conversation. Whether we can hold our cultural traditions in one hand and our children’s futures in the other and find a way to honour both. The dead can teach. Let them teach.

items.title: Allemagne : près de 140 milliards pour la défense, un réarmement qui inquiète même l'Europe
items.description: Au terme d'une nuit de negociations, la coalition de Friedrich Merz a fait passer son projet devant la commission budgetaire du Bundestag. L'adoption definitive reste prevue entre le 24 et le 27 novembre. Le ministere de la Defense se verrait attribuer 109,75 milliards d'euros, contre 82,7 milliards prevus pour 2026. Boris Pistorius, ministre allemand de la Defense, pourrait compter sur pres de 30 milliards d'euros supplementaires tires du fonds special de la Bundeswehr, l'armee allemande. Le gouvernement veut emprunter 122,97 milliards d'euros dans le budget federal. Avec les fonds speciaux, la dette nouvelle atteindrait 210,4 milliards, selon Reuters. Les depenses de defense profitent d'une derogation aux regles allemandes limitant l'endettement public. Ce choix ne fait pas l'unanimite. Le 9 septembre, lors du debat budgetaire, le depute Dietmar Bartsch attaquait cette course aux credits militaires : « Votre demesure n'apporte pas de securite. Vous mettez en peril la paix interieure de notre pays. » Les voisins sur leurs gardes Les reserves ne datent pas du vote du 13 novembre. Le 19 septembre deja, le Wall Street Journal decrivait l'inquietude de voisins de l'Allemagne devant la place qu'une Bundeswehr renforcee pourrait occuper en Europe. En France, ce sont aussi les interets industriels qui sont en jeu. Les commandes de Berlin pourraient favoriser ses fabricants d'armes face aux groupes francais. Le 8 juin, Paris et Berlin avaient d'ailleurs annonce l'arret de leur projet commun d'avion de combat, au cœur du systeme de combat aerien du futur (SCAF), apres des desaccords entre Airbus et Dassault Aviation. En Pologne, le ministre des Affaires etrangeres Radoslaw Sikorski s'etait dit favorable, en septembre, au renforcement de la Bundeswehr, mais il s'inquietait de ce qu'il adviendrait de cette armee si le parti d'extreme droite Alternative pour l'Allemagne (AfD) accedait un jour au pouvoir. a Vienne, le 12 novembre, Dmitri Poliansky, representant permanent de la Russie aupres de l'Organisation pour la securite et la cooperation en Europe (OSCE), a critique l'extension des infrastructures de l'Organisation du traite de l'Atlantique nord (OTAN) pres des frontieres russes. Ses propos portaient sur la militarisation de l'Europe, et non sur ce budget. Le diplomate a prevenu : « Cependant, une seule chose reste incomprehensible : pourquoi les responsables europeens pensent-ils que nous allons assister a tout cela les bras croises ? »

items.title: Grodital launches in Ghana to help users monetise knowledge
items.description: Ghanaian entrepreneur Asante Theophilus Koranteng has launched Grodital, a digital platform designed to help people earn from their knowledge through digital products and affiliate marketing. The platform was officially unveiled on Saturday, 7 November 2026, at The Next Digital Wealth Summit 2026, held at Tomreik Hotel in East Legon, Accra. Grodital was introduced by its Founder and CEO, Asante Theophilus Koranteng, widely known as ATKuniverse. He hosted the summit and used the occasion to present the platform to an audience of creators, marketers, entrepreneurs and students. More than 130 people attended. A summit built around three words The one-day summit was held under the theme ‘Build, Distribute, Evolve’. Each word formed the basis of a panel session, focusing on how to create digital products, reach customers and grow sustainable businesses. The summit featured three panel sessions: ‘How to Turn What You Know Into Something People Would Pay For’, ‘What Separates Top Marketers From Everyone Else’ and ‘What Skills Will Be Relevant in the Next 5 Years’. Six speakers also shared insights centred on the summit’s foundational pillars. In his opening keynote, ATKuniverse argued that Ghana is not short of knowledge. What is rare, he said, is the ability to turn that knowledge into income. He pointed to the numbers. Ghana had about 24.3 million internet users at the start of 2025, representing roughly 70 per cent of the population, according to DataReportal. He also cited Bank of Ghana data showing that mobile money transactions reached GH¢4.54 trillion in 2025, an increase of 50.8 per cent on the previous year. “Having internet access is one thing. Turning it into economic value is another,” he told the audience. What Grodital does Grodital brings three groups of people onto one platform. Creators, coaches and business owners can build and sell digital products such as courses and e-books, set their own prices and manage their sales. Marketers can discover products, join affiliate programmes, obtain unique promotional links and earn commissions on the sales they generate. They do not need to have products of their own to get started. Learners, meanwhile, can use the Study Hub, a learning space offering educational resources and structured courses. ATK describes Grodital as an ecosystem rather than just a marketplace. “The creator has something to offer. The marketer has the ability to distribute it. The learner has the opportunity to acquire knowledge and develop value of their own,” he said. The problem behind the platform ATK said the idea came from watching skilled people create products but struggle to sell them. They needed one tool to host their products, another for sales pages, another to manage customers and yet another to run affiliate programmes. He also said he had personally experienced the challenges. “I built Grodital because I got tired of watching that happen. To other people and, honestly, to myself,” he said. “I didn’t just want to build another website where people could upload products. I wanted to build an ecosystem.” He was clear that the goal goes beyond making a first sale. “There’s a difference between making money online and building a digital business. One can be an activity. The other requires systems.” The wider ambition is to make it easier for people across Africa to participate in the digital economy as creators, entrepreneurs, educators and marketers, rather than only as consumers. The launch moment The reveal came midway through the programme, when the Grodital name reappeared, although some members of the audience had seen it before. ATK also shared a story about his struggles in college and his desire to change things. The event featured an Awards and Recognition segment and closed with a networking session. The company’s motto, repeated from the stage, is “Grow Digitally, Earn Globally.” “What you’re seeing today is not the end of the journey,” ATK said. “It’s the beginning of a much bigger one.” How to get started Grodital is now open to creators, affiliate marketers and learners. Accounts can be created at grodital.com ⁠. Quick facts Event: The Next Digital Wealth Summit 2026 and Grodital Official Launch Date: Saturday, 7 November 2026 Venue: Tomreik Hotel, East Legon, Accra, Ghana Summit theme: Build. Distribute. Evolve. Platform launched: Grodital What it is: A digital commerce and affiliate marketing platform for creators, marketers and learners. Founder and CEO: Asante Theophilus Koranteng (ATKuniverse) Guiding line: “Build what people need. Market what people want.” Website: grodital.com ⁠ Sign-up: grodital.com/signup ⁠ About Grodital Grodital is a digital commerce and affiliate marketing platform built in Ghana. Creators use it to sell digital products, courses and e-books. Marketers use it to promote those products and earn commissions. Learners use its Study Hub to develop new skills. The platform launched on 7 November 2026 and is available at grodital.com ⁠. About the founder Asante Theophilus Koranteng, known professionally as ATKuniverse, is the Founder and CEO of Grodital and the host of The Next Digital Wealth Summit. He built Grodital after years of watching skilled people struggle to turn what they know into income. His aim, he says, is to give creators, marketers and learners one connected platform to make that possible.

items.title: UN chief urges drastic emissions cuts as COP31 wrestles with fossil fuels
items.description: ANTALYA, Turkey, Nov 13 (Reuters) - UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres on Friday called for an "immediate and drastic reduction" in greenhouse gas emissions, as divisions over fossil fuels dominated the first week of COP31 climate talks in Turkey. Big fossil fuel producers and consumers at the talks are resisting any deal that would specify firm new targets or a shift away from oil, gas and coal, observers said as the first week of talks drew to a close.

items.title: DGE : Mohamed Aly Condé prend les commandes de l’institution, avec les élections régionales et sénatoriales en ligne de mire
items.description: Nommé à la tête de la Direction générale des élections (DGE), Mohamed Aly Condé a officiellement pris fonction ce vendredi 13 novembre 2026. La cérémonie d'installation, présidée par la Ministre de l'Administration du territoire et de la Décentralisation, Djénabou Touré, s'est déroulée dans les locaux de l'institution, en présence du Vérificateur général adjoint de la République, de l'inspecteur général du MATD et de plusieurs autres invités. Le nouveau patron de la DGE hérite d'une institution confrontée à d'importantes échéances électorales, notamment les élections régionales annoncées pour le 29 novembre et les élections sénatoriales prévues en décembre. Juriste de formation et ancien conseiller juridique de Djénabou Touré , le nouveau responsable de la DGE n'est pas en terrain inconnu. Il a notamment travaillé aux côtés de l’actuelle Ministre de l’Administration du Territoire et de la Décentralisation dans la conduite de plusieurs processus électoraux, notamment le référendum, l'élection présidentielle ainsi que les élections législatives et communales couplées. C'est d'ailleurs sur la base de cette expérience professionnelle que la Ministre explique avoir proposé son nom au président de la République, Mamadi Doumbouya, qui a entériné cette proposition par décret. « Monsieur Mohamed Aly Condé est un juriste chevronné. Il a servi à mes côtés en tant que conseiller juridique. Un professionnel très engagé, très patriotique », a souligné Djénabou Touré, qui dit avoir confiance en ses capacités à conduire les destinées de cette institution stratégique. Un baptême du feu sous pression, avec des échéances électorales imminentes Si la Ministre se montre confiante quant aux compétences de son ancien collaborateur, elle n'a pas manqué de lui rappeler les exigences et les difficultés liées à ses nouvelles responsabilités. Pour Djénabou Touré, diriger la DGE est loin d'être une mission de tout repos, notamment en raison des nombreuses pressions auxquelles son responsable sera confronté. Elle en a identifié plusieurs sources : les exigences internes de l'administration électorale, les attentes des candidats, les sollicitations des autorités, les réactions de la population et, enfin, la vigilance de la presse et de la société civile. « Un travail qui n'est pas facile, mais si vous vous adressez à la loi, au règlement, votre travail sera facile », a-t-elle conseillé au nouveau directeur général. La Ministre a particulièrement insisté sur la nécessité de préserver l'indépendance professionnelle de la DGE dans l'exécution de ses missions, en évitant toute influence susceptible de compromettre l'équité du processus électoral. « Ne faites pas ce qui est bon pour un candidat, ne faites pas ce qui est bon pour Madame la Ministre, mais faites ce qui est juste et bon pour notre pays », a-t-elle martelé. Un message qui résume, selon elle, l'esprit dans lequel Mohamed Aly Condé devra exercer ses nouvelles fonctions : privilégier l'intérêt supérieur de la Guinée et veiller au respect strict des textes qui encadrent les opérations électorales. Dans cette perspective, Djénabou Touré l'a également exhorté à maintenir un dialogue permanent avec les différentes parties prenantes, notamment les acteurs politiques, les organisations de la société civile et les médias. Elle l'a notamment invité à ne pas fermer les portes de son institution aux critiques et aux interpellations. « Ils vont vous suivre comme des gendarmes qui vous poseront des questions, ne leur fermez surtout pas votre porte, écoutez-les », a-t-elle recommandé, en évoquant particulièrement le rôle de la presse dans le suivi du processus électoral. Sur le plan managérial, la ministre a appelé le nouveau patron de la DGE à faire preuve de leadership, à éviter la formation de clans au sein de l'administration et à privilégier la compétence et le mérite dans la gestion de ses collaborateurs. Elle a également insisté sur la nécessité de travailler en étroite collaboration avec son adjoint, présenté comme un spécialiste des questions électorales et logistiques. Elle l'a invité à déléguer les responsabilités, à donner des instructions claires et à assurer leur suivi et leur évaluation. Ces recommandations interviennent alors que la DGE doit rapidement se mobiliser pour les prochaines échéances électorales. La Ministre a notamment évoqué les élections régionales, annoncées pour le 29 novembre, ainsi que les élections sénatoriales prévues en décembre. « Je suis convaincue qu'avec son adjoint, qui est aussi un professionnel, un spécialiste des questions électorales, logistiques, ensemble ils pourront finaliser le reste du processus », a-t-elle assuré. Mohamed Aly Condé mise sur la continuité, la transparence et la performance Prenant la parole après son installation, Mohamed Aly Condé a d'abord exprimé sa reconnaissance au Président de la République, Mamadi Doumbouya, pour la confiance placée en sa personne. Conscient de la portée de cette nomination, il a tenu à préciser que cette responsabilité dépasse le cadre d'une simple promotion professionnelle. « Cette nomination n'est pas simplement une promotion personnelle, elle constitue avant tout un appel à servir davantage la nation, à répondre aux attentes des citoyens, à contribuer avec loyauté et détermination à la consolidation des institutions de notre pays », a-t-il déclaré. Le nouveau Directeur Général a également rendu un hommage appuyé à Djénabou Touré pour son accompagnement et son encadrement durant son passage au poste de conseiller juridique. Il a salué les réformes engagées et les résultats obtenus sous son impulsion à la tête de la DGE, estimant que ces acquis constituent un héritage institutionnel qu'il entend préserver et consolider. « Je ne viens pas effacer un héritage, mais le préserver, le consolider et l'élever davantage », a-t-il assuré. Mohamed Aly Condé entend ainsi inscrire son action dans une dynamique de continuité, tout en accélérant les réformes et en améliorant les performances de l'institution. Sur le fond, il a rappelé que la DGE occupe une place déterminante dans le fonctionnement de l'État et dans la consolidation de l'architecture démocratique du pays. À ce titre, il estime que la confiance des citoyens dans les institutions dépend notamment de la qualité de l'organisation des élections, de la transparence des opérations, de la fiabilité des résultats et du respect des dispositions légales. Il a ainsi défini les principaux piliers de son action : la neutralité administrative, l'impartialité, la rigueur professionnelle, la redevabilité et le respect de la loi. « Notre responsabilité est d'organiser des élections crédibles, transparentes, inclusives, apaisées et conformes aux textes en vigueur », a-t-il affirmé. Les élections régionales et sénatoriales, premières grandes priorités Dans son allocution, l e nouveau directeur général a pris l'engagement de mobiliser son équipe afin que les élections régionales et sénatoriales se déroulent dans les meilleures conditions possibles. Pour y parvenir, il entend miser sur l'anticipation, la planification, la coordination, le contrôle et l'évaluation de chaque étape du processus électoral. « Nous n'avons pas le droit à l'improvisation. Nous devons anticiper, planifier, coordonner, contrôler et évaluer chaque étape du processus », a-t-il insisté. Il a également annoncé sa volonté de travailler en étroite collaboration avec l'ensemble des acteurs concernés : autorités administratives, acteurs politiques, candidats et organisations de la société civile. Le nouveau patron de la DGE entend faire de son institution un espace ouvert au dialogue et à la concertation, sans pour autant renoncer à son professionnalisme et à son impartialité dans la conduite des opérations électorales. Un appel à la mobilisation des cadres et agents de la DGE S'adressant particulièrement aux cadres et agents de la Direction générale des élections, Mohamed Aly Condé a lancé un appel à la cohésion, à la discipline et au renforcement de l'engagement collectif. Tout en reconnaissant l'expérience et les compétences déjà acquises par les travailleurs de l'institution, il a tenu à les rassurer sur sa volonté de ne pas remettre en cause le travail accompli. « Je ne viens pas bouleverser le travail accompli, encore moins remettre en cause les compétences existantes. Je viens m'inscrire dans une dynamique de continuité, de consolidation et de performance », a-t-il précisé. Il a, dans le même esprit, promis de rester ouvert aux initiatives et propositions constructives, tout en attendant de ses collaborateurs loyauté institutionnelle, discipline, rigueur, intégrité et professionnalisme. Son ambition, a-t-il indiqué, est de faire de la DGE une référence nationale et internationale en matière d'administration et de gestion électorale. Au terme de son intervention, le nouveau Directeur Général a réaffirmé sa volonté de travailler avec toutes les compétences disponibles et de faire du résultat le principal indicateur de son action. Avec cette prise de fonction, Mohamed Aly Condé hérite ainsi d'une responsabilité majeure : poursuivre le travail engagé à la tête de la DGE, tout en conduisant les prochaines échéances électorales dans un climat de transparence, de confiance et d'apaisement.
